confirmed.violation: Rule 164.2.b defines a Basic Rune's recycle ability as "Recycle this: [Reaction] — Add [C]" — recycling adds exactly one Power of the rune's Domain and nothing else (Energy is produced only by the separate exhaust ability, 164.2.a). In this trace every recycleRune action on a Basic Rune adds +1 Energy in addition to +1 domain Power, giving the player double resources from a single recycle.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/resources.ts:196 — pre-754016c reducer had `pool.energy += 1;` (already fixed in commit 754016c)
confirmed.notes:
Rule 164.2.b verbatim: "Recycle this: [Reaction] — Add [C]", with 164.2.b.1 clarifying the Power added corresponds to the recycled Rune's Domain. Energy comes only from the separate exhaust ability 164.2.a ("[E]: [Reaction] — Add [1]"). So a Basic Rune recycle must add exactly 1 domain Power and 0 Energy.

Trace evidence checks out (before→after pool deltas from adjacent seq entries in game-r2-11.jsonl):
- seq 6→7 (turn 2, player-2 recycleRune chaos): {energy:3,{}} → {energy:4,{chaos:1}} — +1 energy illegally.
- seq 17→18 (turn 4 first action, pool emptied per rule 167): {0,{}} → {energy:1,{chaos:1}} — +1 energy illegally.
- seq 29→30 (turn 5, player-1 recycleRune mind): {energy:1,{}} → {energy:2,{mind:1}} — +1 energy illegally.
Holds across both players and all four Basic Rune domains, so not a card passive.

Source confirms: git show 754016c on resources.ts shows the pre-fix reducer contained `pool.energy += 1;` alongside the power increment. That line was removed in commit 754016c ("fix(rules-via-ui): loop rounds 1-3 — 9 rule bugs (… 164.2.b …)", 2026-08-04). Current HEAD (resources.ts:192-198) is rule-correct. The trace was produced by a build predating 754016c and exhibits the violation exactly as claimed.

confirmed.violation: Rule 460: "A Combat occurs when a Cleanup occurs, there are no items on the Chain, there is a staged Combat at a Battlefield, and no Showdown or Combat is ongoing at any other Battlefield." Combined with 461 (staged = opposing units present), combat initiation is mandatory at the next Cleanup once staged. The engine instead treats it as deferred/optional: after a move stages combat, it returns to Neutral Open and offers arbitrary main-phase actions (rune generation, playUnit, further standardMoves to OTHER battlefields) with `startShowdown` merely one option among many.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:334 (combatPending computed but never consumed); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:885-929 (startShowdown still discretionary); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/movement.ts:452-479 (gankingMove lacks the 323.13 auto-open that standardMove got in 0396770)
confirmed.notes:
Rule reading is correct: 460 + 319.8 (Cleanup after every Move) + 323.13 ("If Neutral Open and Combats are Staged, the Turn Player chooses one … Combat begins there") make combat initiation mandatory, not discretionary. Trace evidence is accurate — game-r2-3.jsonl seq 44→45 and seq 115→117 show Neutral Open (chain=null, showdownStack=[]) with a contested bf holding opposing units, yet recycleRune/playUnit/activateAbility/standardMove are offered alongside startShowdown, and at seq 117 a second standardMove opens a non-combat showdown at a DIFFERENT bf while combat is still staged at p1-bf.

However the trace (mtime Aug 4 00:12Z) predates commit 0396770 (Aug 4 01:01Z, "rules 319.8/323.13/344/450 - standardMove opens showdown mandatorily"), which patched movement.ts:335-350 to auto-open a (combat) showdown inside the standardMove reducer when bf.controller !== mover. On current HEAD the exact seq 44→45 / 115→116 sequence would not reproduce — standardMove now leaves the game in Showdown Open, so the neutral-open guards on other moves block them.

The fix is a local patch, not general 323.13 enforcement: performCleanup computes `combatPending` (state-based-checks.ts:334) but nothing consumes it (grep confirms zero non-test consumers); startShowdown (chain-moves.ts:885-929) is still an optional enumerator entry; gankingMove's reducer (movement.ts:452-479) neither sets contested nor opens a showdown and doesn't gate on neutral-open; riftbound-flow.ts has no staged-combat forcing. So any path that stages combat other than standardMove (ganking, effect-driven placement, hunt) still returns to Neutral Open with startShowdown as one option among many. Verdict PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because the specific cited evidence is stale vs HEAD; the residual violation exists via other paths but is not demonstrated by this trace.

confirmed.violation: Rule 465.2 makes the Combat Damage Step a mandatory Outstanding Task: "When the Showdown closes, Attackers and Defenders resolve Combat Damage." In the trace, when a Combat Showdown closes (both players pass), the engine does NOT proceed to damage — it drops back to a choice state offering BOTH `startShowdown` (reopen the same showdown) and `resolveFullCombat` as optional player moves, plus unrelated actions. This lets the turn player loop the same Combat Showdown indefinitely and interleave non-combat actions between showdown-close and damage.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:905 (startShowdown condition lacks !bf.showdownComplete) and packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/combat.ts:227 (resolveFullCombat offered as optional move instead of forced Outstanding Task after showdown close at chain-moves.ts:838)
confirmed.notes: Rule text matches the claim: 348.1 says when a Combat Showdown closes "proceed with the remaining steps of Combat to resolve the phase", and 465.1/465.2 make Combat Damage an Outstanding (mandatory) Task. The engine does not honor this. In chain-moves.ts:833-838 the passShowdownFocus reducer, on combat-showdown close, only sets bf.showdownComplete=true and drops back to neutral-open; resolveFullCombat (combat.ts:227-256) is then merely enumerated as an optional move gated on contested && showdownComplete, while startShowdown (chain-moves.ts:885-929) re-enumerates because its condition only checks bf.contested (line 905/925) and never excludes showdownComplete. This is a genuine 465.2/348.1 violation and an infinite-loop vector.

confirmed.violation: Rule 448 (via 144.4.b) permits a Unit's Standard Move from a Battlefield to its controller's Base; 144.4.c.1/810 additionally permits Battlefield→Battlefield for units with Ganking. In this trace the engine NEVER enumerates any standardMove option for a unit whose origin is a Battlefield — the only destinations ever offered are the two battlefield IDs, and only for units currently at Base. Ready units sitting on a Battlefield across multiple Awaken cycles get zero standardMove options, so the legal BF→Base retreat (and any BF→BF gank) is unreachable.

A Showdown/Combat begins there." The only player agency is WHICH battlefield; opening is not discretionary.

confirmed.violation: Rule 308.1: if a Combat is in progress the turn is in a Showdown State (308.1.a: only Action/Reaction playable). After the combat Showdown closes but before combat resolution, the engine drops showdownStack to [] and treats the turn as Neutral Open — offering playUnit, recycleRune, and both `startShowdown`/`resolveFullCombat` as free choices — even though Combat is still in progress at the contested battlefield.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/chain/chain-state.ts:131 (getTurnState ignores in-progress Combat / contested battlefields); downstream gate: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:360
confirmed.notes:
Rule 308.1 verbatim: "If a Showdown or Combat is in progress, the turn is in a Showdown State"; 308.1.a: only Action/Reaction playable in Showdown State. Rule 316.7.e/f: Combat is a multi-step procedure that *includes* a Showdown as one step — Combat remains in progress after its Showdown closes until the resolution step clears it.

Engine: getTurnState() (chain-state.ts:131-146) computes turn state from showdownStack + chain ONLY — it never inspects whether a Combat is in progress (any battlefield.contested===true). So once passShowdownFocus pops showdownStack to [], getTurnState returns "neutral-open" even though the contested battlefield's Combat has not resolved. Every Discretionary-Action gate (playUnit cards.ts:360, startShowdown chain-moves.ts:868, resolveFullCombat combat.ts:233) keys off that value, so they all become optional side-by-side.

Trace game-r2-11.jsonl confirms: seq 116 both players passShowdownFocus → post-state showdownStack=[], bf player-1-bf-ogn-275-298 still {contested:true, units:[P2-main-22, P1-main-10]}. seq 117 available = {concede, playUnit(sfd-061-221→base), recycleRune, resolveFullCombat, startShowdown}; P1 chose playUnit — a standard (non-Ambush, non-Action/Reaction) unit play mid-combat, illegal under 308.1.a. seq 120 same menu shape. Also startShowdown re-enumerates for the same battlefield after showdownComplete, letting the player loop the Showdown Step instead of proceeding rigidly through 463's steps.

(recycleRune alone may be defensible — rule 594 allows recycling at any time and it appears during active showdowns too — but playUnit + a second startShowdown alongside an optional resolveFullCombat are concrete 308.1 violations.)

confirmed.violation: Rule 343.1 says the turn is in a Showdown State whenever a Showdown *or Combat* is in progress. Between a combat-showdown close and combat resolution, Combat is still in progress, so the turn must remain in Showdown State. confirmed.notes:
Rule 343.1 verbatim: "The turn is said to be in a Showdown State if a Showdown or Combat is in progress." Rules 463–466 define Combat as three ordered steps (Combat Showdown → Combat Damage → Resolution), and 348.1 directs that when a Combat Showdown closes the game "proceed[s] with the remaining steps of Combat." So between the combat-showdown close and the Damage/Resolution steps, Combat is unambiguously still in progress and the turn must remain in Showdown State.

Engine: getTurnState() (chain/chain-state.ts:131–146) derives state solely from interaction.showdownStack + interaction.chain; it has no Combat-in-progress input. passShowdownFocus reducer (chain-moves.ts:807–850) on all-passed for a combat showdown sets bf.showdownComplete=true then calls endShowdownState() (chain-state.ts:466) which pops the showdown → showdownStack=[]. getTurnState() therefore returns "neutral-open" while a contested battlefield still awaits resolveFullCombat. resolveFullCombat's own condition (combat.ts:233) and startShowdown's condition (chain-moves.ts:868) both explicitly require neutral-open, cementing the mismodel.

Trace game-r2-0.jsonl seq 170–174 matches exactly: seq 171 both players have passed → showdownStack=[] while player-2-bf still contested=true; seq 172 available includes activateAbility×4, startShowdown, resolveFullCombat with showdownStack=[]; player-1 picks activateAbility, chain-18 opens in neutral-closed; seq 174 chain resolves back to neutral-open with priority still on player-1. Per 343.1 this window should be Showdown State (so 343.1.a/b default-play restrictions and 344's neutral-open precondition for startShowdown would bar the extra options, and 348.1 mandates proceeding directly to the Damage Step rather than granting free neutral-open priority).

Minor caveat on the sub-claim: rule 346/340.2.a's focus-pass wording is "during a Showdown", and the Showdown itself has closed per 348 — so the focus-never-passed argument leans on 346 more than the text strictly supports. The core 343.1 violation (Neutral reported while Combat in progress, unlocking startShowdown/free chains before damage) stands independently.

The rules reading is correct (319.8 makes Cleanup outstanding after every Move; 323.9 stages Combat; 323.13 mandatorily begins that Combat during the same Cleanup while still in Neutral Open; 320.1 forbids awarding Priority during Cleanup — so no second discretionary standardMove may intervene). And the trace evidence is real: at seq 115 p2 standardMove main-6→p1-bf leaves p1-bf {controller=player-1, contested=true, units=3×p1+1×p2} with interaction.showdownStack=[], and at seq 116-117 standardMove is offered/executed again. Current movement.ts:335-350 unconditionally calls startShowdownState (combat=hasOpponentUnit) inside the bf.controller!==playerId branch, so getTurnState leaves neutral-open immediately and standardMove.condition (movement.ts:149) rejects a second move. No live bug at HEAD.

The claim misreads the governing rule and proposes a rules-incorrect outcome.

(1) Rule text: 323.11 does say Contested is only removed when the contesting player has no units — that part of the claim is accurate. But the claim ignores rule 348.2.a, which explicitly governs Non-Combat Showdown closure: "If only one player's Units remain at the Battlefield, and if that player does not already Control the Battlefield, that player establishes Control over the Battlefield" (348.2.a.1: this is a Conquer). The correct rules outcome for the traced scenario is mandatory control establishment for player-2, NOT "Contested remains and 323.12 re-stages another Showdown". The claim's proposed correct behavior would produce an infinite showdown loop and directly contradicts 348.2.a.

(2) Source: chain-moves.ts:813-847 (passShowdownFocus reducer, non-combat branch) implements 348.2.a — when isCombatShowdown=false and owners.size===1, it sets bf.controller=solo and awards the Conquer VP. The engine does not model 323.11 as a step that "clears" contested here at all.

(3) Trace: game-r2-6.jsonl seq 204-208 shows contested=false at every step including seq=204/205 while the showdown was still active. So the engine never "cleared" Contested at cleanup step 8 — it was never true in the recorded state. The claim's factual premise ("engine clears Contested") is not supported by the evidence.

There may be a separate 348.2.a issue (auto-conquer didn't fire in this trace — controller stayed null and conquerBattlefield was offered as optional), but that is a different rule, a different mechanism, and not what this claim asserts.

Rule 313.3 is not the governing rule for Focus after chain resolution, and the engine does not violate it.

(1) Rule text: 313.3 says only "A player who passes Priority retains Focus." The trace respects this — at seq=21 player-1 passes chain Priority and post-state focusPlayer is still 'player-1'. Focus changes at seq=22 not because a player passed Priority, but because the last chain item resolved. That transition is governed by rule 346, not 313.3.

(2) Rule 346 (Chains & Showdowns): "When the last item on the chain resolves and the turn returns to an Open State during a Showdown, Focus passes, and the next Player gains both Focus and Priority." The engine implements exactly this at chain-state.ts:325-338 (resolveTopItem). So the claim's core assertion — that Focus must never transfer on chain resolution — is contrary to the rules.
